steps.body: When both factors are two-digit, both split — and the rectangle gains four regions instead of two.
steps.narration: When both factors are two-digit, both split — and the rectangle gains four regions instead of two.

widget.prompt: Build the 23 × 14 rectangle: 23 wide and 14 tall.
widget.successFeedback: 322 — and it divides into 200, 80, 30 and 12, which are the four partial products.
widget.lowFeedback: Smaller than 322 — keep building until both sides reach 23 and 14.
widget.highFeedback: Larger than 322 — a side has grown past the factors named.
widget.factorFeedback: That area is right, but the sides are not — this model must measure 23 across and 14 down.

predict.prompt: Splitting both factors of 23 × 14, how many regions appear?
predict.reveal: Two pieces across times two pieces down makes four rectangles, and all four are real area.

cml.actionGoal: Split a factor into places, build each piece, and reassemble the whole for g4m 2x2 area.
invariants: Splitting a factor never changes the product: every piece of the split multiplies the other factor, and the pieces add back to exactly the same total, which is what makes g4m 2x2 area decomposable at all.
misconceptions: Adding only some of the partial products, dropping or inventing a zero when factors carry tens, or letting a remainder reach or exceed the divisor.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one partial product were left out, exactly how much of the total would go missing?

widget.prompt: Use an area model for 38 × 17. What is the product?

commonErrors.feedback: That added only the corner pieces — the two middle rectangles were left out of the total.
That is only the tens row of the model; the ones row still has to join it.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Split a factor into its places, multiply each part, and add every piece back.

widget.prompt: Which four partial products build the area model for 29 × 19?

options.feedback: Correct — both factors split, so the rectangle has four regions and every pairing appears once.

options.label: 20×10 and 9×9
options.feedback: Only the two corner regions. The 20×9 and 9×10 rectangles are real area too.

options.label: 29×10 and 29×9
options.feedback: That splits only one factor — a valid method, but not the FOUR-region model this asks for.
Two of those multiply a factor's own pieces together, which no side of the rectangle measures.
